You are a worker running a verification-only FULL gate for the Fortress clean-ladder rebuild. Background: the coordinator has just rewritten the `clean-ladder` branch history locally (dropping the commit that tracked generated sources and ignoring those paths instead); your job is solely to prove the rewritten tip builds and tests fully green from a tree with NO pre-existing generated sources. You make NO commits, NO pushes, and NO edits — gate and report only.

Read `/home/user/fortress/explorations/rebuild-plan.md` sections "Worktree and environment mechanics" and "Gate definitions" before acting.

State in place (verified by the coordinator):
- Worktree `/home/user/fortress-clean`, branch `clean-ladder`, local tip `a92f1b736` "Bump Scala from 2.10.7 to 2.12.20" (do not compare against the remote — it intentionally differs until the coordinator pushes).
- The generated sources (ASTGen `nodes/`, four Rats! parsers, Operators.java, FortressAst.scala, Library/FortressAst.fsi/.fss) are ABSENT from both the tree and the index, and their paths are now in `.gitignore`. The build must regenerate them.

Your duties:
1. FULL gate on JDK 8. Inline env in every command: `export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-8-openjdk-amd64 && export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH && export FORTRESS_HOME=/home/user/fortress-clean && unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS && cd /home/user/fortress-clean && ant ...`. Sequence: `ant clean compileAll` (expect green; this run regenerates all generated sources from scratch), then `ant testFast` (expect sum 1,377 tests / 47 suites / 0F / 0E across 4 tracks), then `ant testSystem` (expect sum 382 / 0F / 0E across 4 shards). Note each target's wall-clock.
2. For the long targets use the established pattern: direct output to scratchpad logs (`b4drop-compile.log`, `b4drop-testfast.log`, `b4drop-testsystem.log` under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/`) and watch with the Monitor tool until "BUILD SUCCESSFUL" or "BUILD FAILED"; never read whole logs — grep/tail only.
3. After all runs: `git status --short` must be EMPTY (this is the point of the exercise — the regenerated sources and all other build exhaust must be fully covered by .gitignore). If anything shows as untracked or modified, list exactly what and stop.
4. Use only scratch filenames prefixed `b4drop-` in the scratchpad. Do not touch the checklist, do not commit, do not push anywhere.

ANY failure, count drift, or non-empty git status: report precisely and stop. Deviations are not yours to resolve.

Report tersely: gate result per target with wall-clock, sums verified, git-status-clean confirmation (or the exact residue), deviations.

Your final text is your report to the coordinator, not prose for a human.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X".
